newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks move lower on thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks move lower on thin trading.

text.p: Cyprus stocks closed marginally lower on Friday after a lacklustre week of trading, losing 0.75 points, or 0.90 percent, during the week.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general share index closed at 82.47 points on Friday from last week's close of 83.22.

CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation, said that most key market players were on the sidelines at present, while liquidity will be absorbed from the market in October when payments on partly-paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus and the Cyprus Popular Bank fall due.
The banking sub index closed at 89.50 points, scoring a marginal drop over last Friday's close of 89.85.
Fully-paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus closed at 339.5, slightly higher than 339 close last week. Fully-paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 317.5, losing 4.5 cents from 322 last week.
The third largest bank, Hellenic, closed at 250 in heavy trading on Friday, where it absorbed 21 percent of all transactions. Last week it closed at 248.5.
The insurance company sub index closed at 60.51, losing 1.37 points over the week.
Universal Life Insurance closed at 374, a fraction lower than last week's 374.5. Paneuropean Insurance lost five cents over the week to close at 136.

Cyprus Airways, the island's state-controlled national carrier, fell to a year-low of 42.5 cents earlier in the week amid new friction between the pilots' union and management over the grounding of a pilot.
It closed at 43 cents on Friday.
